videos.title: What Is System Design? HLD vs LLD Explained
videos.summary: What is system design, really? In this first lesson you'll learn how requirements turn into an architecture, the difference between High-Level Design (HLD) and Low-Level Design (LLD), and what interviewers actually evaluate in a system design interview.
chapters: 0:45 Example: a FastAPI app on one server

videos.title: Client-Server & Multi-Tier Architecture Explained (1, 2, 3 & N-Tier)
videos.summary: Why is almost every app split into layers? In this lesson you'll learn the client-server model and how single-tier, two-tier, three-tier and N-tier architectures differ. You'll also see why each tier scales on its own, and what happens when one tier becomes the bottleneck.
chapters: 1:55 When one tier becomes the bottleneck

videos.title: Functional Requirements in System Design (URL Shortener & Chat App Examples)
videos.summary: The fastest way to fail a system design interview is to start drawing boxes too early. Step one is functional requirements: what the system must do.
chapters: 1:09 Rule of thumb: 3–5 core use cases

videos.title: Non-Functional Requirements Explained: p99 Latency, 99.9% Uptime
videos.summary: Two systems can have exactly the same features and still need completely different architectures. The difference is the non-functional requirements (NFRs).

videos.title: System Design Trade-offs: How to Justify Any Design Choice (Eventual Consistency, Caching)
videos.summary: In system design there is no free lunch. Every choice improves one quality attribute and costs another. This lesson shows you how to talk about trade-offs like a senior engineer.
chapters: 2:03 Answering: a real trade-off you made

videos.title: Vertical Scaling Explained: When to Scale Up (and Its 4 Limits)
videos.summary: Your server is maxed out. The quickest fix is often to get a bigger machine. That's vertical scaling, also called scaling up.
chapters: 1:30 Limits 3 & 4: single point of failure and downtime
1:48 When scaling up is the right move

videos.title: Horizontal Scaling Explained: Stateless Services, Autoscaling
videos.summary: One machine always hits a ceiling. Horizontal scaling (scaling out) adds more machines behind a load balancer instead.
chapters: 0:00 From one big machine to many
0:14 Scale out: many copies + a load balancer
0:51 Move state out of the servers
1:49 Why databases are harder to scale out

videos.title: Latency Explained: p99, Latency Budgets & Numbers Everyone Should Know
videos.summary: You click a button and you wait. That wait is latency, the most visible number in any system.
chapters: 2:10 Over budget? Find the part, apply the fix

videos.title: Throughput & Little's Law Explained: RPS, Concurrency and Latency at 100%
videos.summary: Latency is how long one car takes on the highway. Throughput is how many cars get through each hour. This lesson shows how the two are connected.
chapters: 0:14 Throughput = work per unit of time

videos.title: Availability Explained: The Nines, MTBF vs MTTR, Series vs Parallel
videos.summary: Your site is down. How do you measure "up", and how do you design for it?

videos.title: Reliability vs Availability vs Durability (Up ≠ Right)
videos.summary: Your banking app loads instantly and returns 200 OK, but shows the wrong balance. It's up. Is it working?

videos.title: Scalability Explained: Load Parameters, Twitter Fan-out & Amdahl's Law
videos.summary: Everyone says their system is "scalable". But what does that really mean, and why do systems stop scaling long before you run out of servers?

videos.title: CAP Theorem Explained Properly (It's NOT "Pick Two") | CP vs AP
videos.summary: "Consistency, availability, partition tolerance: pick two." It's catchy, and it's misleading. Here's what the CAP theorem actually says.
chapters: 1:01 The real theorem (and why "CA" isn't real)

videos.title: PACELC Theorem Explained: CAP's Missing Half (Latency vs Consistency)
videos.summary: CAP tells you what happens during a network partition, but partitions are rare. PACELC covers the other 99% of the time.

videos.title: Consistency Models Explained: Linearizable vs Causal vs Eventual
videos.summary: Consistency isn't a yes/no question. It's a spectrum, from strong guarantees that cost a lot to weak ones that are cheap and fast.

videos.title: Fault Tolerance Explained: Fault vs Failure, AZ & Blast Radius
videos.summary: Disks die, networks drop packets, and someone pushes a bad config at 5 pm on a Friday. Things will break. The question is whether your users notice.

videos.title: Single Point of Failure (SPOF) Explained: Active-Passive vs Active-Active
videos.summary: A chain of strong links fails at its weakest one. In system design, that weak link is a single point of failure (SPOF).

videos.title: Simple Beats Clever: Cost, Performance & Complexity (YAGNI, TCO, CPR)
videos.summary: It's tempting to design like a big tech company on day one: shards, queues, caches and microservices. But every box has a price.

videos.title: Stateless vs Stateful: Sessions, Sticky Sessions & Scaling WebSockets
videos.summary: Your chat app works on one server. Add a second server, and some messages never arrive. The code isn't broken. The problem is state.
chapters: 0:50 Making a service stateless (Redis vs sticky sessions)

videos.title: OSI Model for System Design: L4 vs L7 Load Balancers & TLS
videos.summary: Interviewers say "L4 load balancer" and "L7 firewall" all the time. This lesson decodes the OSI model and shows which layers actually matter in system design.
chapters: 0:00 What happens when you type a URL
0:51 L3, L4 and L7: the three that matter

videos.title: TCP/IP Model: What Happens When You Type a URL?
videos.summary: The internet doesn't run on the 7-layer OSI model. It runs on TCP/IP. This lesson maps the two and follows one HTTPS request from a laptop to a cloud VM.
chapters: 0:00 OSI vs what the internet runs on
1:12 Typing a URL: DNS + TCP handshake
2:22 The cost before the first byte

videos.title: TCP Explained: ACKs, Flow & Congestion Control, HOL Blocking
videos.summary: IP loses, duplicates and reorders packets, yet your database results always arrive complete and in order. That's TCP. This lesson shows how it does it, and what it costs.
chapters: 1:08 Congestion control: slow start, CUBIC, BBR
1:49 HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and DB connection pools

videos.title: TCP Handshake, FIN/RST & TIME_WAIT: Running Out of Ports
videos.summary: "Cannot assign requested address." CPU is fine, but your service has run out of ports. This lesson explains how TCP connections open and close, and why lots of short-lived connections cause port exhaustion.
chapters: 1:27 Port exhaustion: the math (and NAT gateways)

videos.title: UDP vs TCP: When Speed Beats Reliability (Voice, Games, QUIC)
videos.summary: On a video call you'd rather lose a few milliseconds of audio than freeze while lost packets are resent. That's UDP. This lesson shows what UDP gives up, what you get in return, and when to pick it over TCP.
chapters: 0:00 Why a video call shouldn't freeze
0:37 Low overhead: header, setup, HOL, multicast

videos.title: IP Addresses, Subnets & CIDR: What Does 10.0.0.0/16 Mean?
videos.summary: In the cloud you design your own address space, and a bad plan is painful to change later. This lesson covers IP addresses, private ranges, NAT, CIDR and subnets, then designs a real two-zone VPC.
chapters: 2:20 Example: a VPC across two zones
2:46 Why databases go in private subnets

videos.title: Ports, Sockets & Routing: How One Port Handles 100k Connections
videos.summary: One server, one port (443), yet 100,000 live WebSocket connections. How? This lesson explains ports, sockets, the connection 5-tuple, and how routers move packets hop by hop.
chapters: 0:15 Ports: IP finds the machine, port finds the process
1:53 Route tables and longest prefix match

videos.title: How DNS Resolution Works: Resolvers, Records, TTL & Migrations
videos.summary: You switch api.example.com to a new load balancer, and an hour later half your users still hit the old one. Nothing is broken: it's DNS caching. This lesson walks through how DNS resolution really works.
chapters: 0:00 Why users still hit the old server
0:44 A lookup on a cold cache: root → TLD → authoritative
1:11 Record types: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS

videos.title: DNS Traffic Management: GeoDNS, Weighted, Failover & Anycast
videos.summary: Two regions: eu-west and us-east. Paris users should land in Europe, New York users in the US, and if Europe goes down everyone should fail over. DNS can do all of this, but it has limits. This lesson shows how.

videos.title: HTTP Fundamentals: Methods, Status Codes, 401 vs 403 & ETags
videos.summary: Every API call is HTTP, and interviewers love the details. Which methods are safe to retry? What's the real difference between 401 and 403? How do ETags save bandwidth? This lesson covers HTTP properly.

videos.title: HTTPS & TLS 1.3 Handshake: ECDHE, Forward Secrecy & 0-RTT
videos.summary: Every padlock in your browser means a TLS handshake just happened. This lesson walks through it step by step: how the server proves who it is, how both sides agree on keys nobody else can see, and where TLS should end in your architecture.
chapters: 1:18 TLS 1.2 vs TLS 1.3 1:43 Session keys, resumption and 0-RTT
2:51 Where TLS ends: the load balancer

videos.title: Certificates & PKI: Chain of Trust, SNI, Let's Encrypt & mTLS
videos.summary: Your site works for 90 days, then every browser shows a red warning: the certificate expired. This lesson explains how certificates work, how browsers decide to trust them, and how to automate rotation so it never happens.
chapters: 0:59 How a browser trusts a certificate

videos.title: HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3: Multiplexing, HOL Blocking & QUIC
videos.summary: A web page can fetch a hundred files, and how those requests share the network decides how fast it feels. This lesson explains what each HTTP version fixed, and why HTTP/3 moved to UDP.
chapters: 0:21 HTTP/1.1: one request at a time

videos.title: WebSockets: Upgrade Handshake, Heartbeats & Scaling to Millions
videos.summary: Chat, live dashboards and multiplayer games need messages in both directions, instantly. WebSockets give you one long-lived, full-duplex connection. This lesson covers how they start, how they stay alive, and how to scale them.

videos.title: SSE vs Long Polling vs WebSockets: How AI Answers Stream
videos.summary: When an AI assistant answers word by word, that's usually server-sent events: one HTTP response that stays open while the server pushes tokens. This lesson compares short polling, long polling, SSE and WebSockets, and shows when to use each.
chapters: 1:31 Example: streaming LLM tokens with FastAPI
1:56 Polling vs long polling vs SSE vs WebSockets

videos.title: HTTP Streaming: Chunked Transfer, Backpressure & gRPC Streams
videos.summary: A user exports five million orders as CSV. Build the file in memory and you need gigabytes of RAM (or crash). Stream it and memory stays flat. This lesson explains how HTTP streaming works and how to do it safely.
chapters: 1:02 Example: streaming a CSV export in FastAPI

videos.title: Forward vs Reverse Proxy: Egress Control, TLS & NGINX
videos.summary: Both are called proxies, but one works for the clients and the other works for the servers. Mixing them up is a classic interview slip. This lesson separates them clearly, with a real NGINX setup.

videos.title: CDNs Explained: Edge PoPs, Cache Keys, Origin Shield & Purges
videos.summary: Your servers are in Virginia; your shopper is in Mumbai. Every image and script crosses the world at ~200 ms per round trip. A CDN brings content close to users. This lesson covers how CDNs work and how to deploy without serving stale files.
chapters: 2:16 Example: images + JS bundles on a CDN

videos.title: Connection Pooling & Keep-Alive: Pool Sizing, Leaks & Timeouts
videos.summary: Your FastAPI service calls a payments API on every request, and under load latency spikes. Often the culprit is one line: a new HTTP client inside every handler. This lesson explains connection reuse, pools, and how to size them.
chapters: 0:23 The cost of a new connection
1:42 How big should the pool be?

videos.title: Network Timeouts: Connect, Read, Deadlines & the Random 502 Bug
videos.summary: A dependency doesn't fail, it just stops answering. Without timeouts, threads pile up, pools drain and your service goes down too. This lesson covers every timeout you need and the classic keep-alive mismatch behind random 502s.
chapters: 1:41 Shrink timeouts as you go deeper

videos.title: REST Principles: Resources, Verbs, HATEOAS & "Cancel Order"
videos.summary: Many "RESTful" APIs are just JSON over HTTP. This lesson explains what REST really means, designs endpoints for an e-commerce service, and answers a classic interview question: how do you model cancel order?
chapters: 0:17 Resources are nouns, methods are verbs

videos.title: GraphQL for System Design: Resolvers, N+1, DataLoader & Limits
videos.summary: A mobile product page needs five REST calls over a slow network. With GraphQL it's one query that returns exactly what the screen needs. This lesson covers how GraphQL works, its classic performance trap, and how to protect your server.
chapters: 0:00 Five REST calls vs one query
0:45 The product page in one query

videos.title: gRPC & Protocol Buffers: .proto, HTTP/2, Deadlines & Evolution
videos.summary: A Python orders service calls a Go inventory service thousands of times per second. Hand-written JSON clients drift, and every call pays for verbose text. This lesson shows how gRPC and protobuf fix that, and why teams use gRPC inside and REST outside.
chapters: 0:00 Python ↔ Go at thousands of calls per second
1:06 HTTP/2, call types, deadlines, status codes

videos.title: REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC: How to Choose an API Style
videos.summary: The interview question isn't "what is gRPC?" It's "which one would you pick, and why?" This lesson compares REST, GraphQL and gRPC on the criteria that matter and shows how real systems use all three.

videos.title: API Resource Modeling & URI Design: Nesting, Actions & Bulk
videos.summary: A good API is predictable: developers can guess the endpoint before reading the docs. This lesson covers URI design rules and the tricky cases interviewers ask about: nested resources, non-CRUD actions and bulk operations.
chapters: 2:21 Why not just PATCH the status?

videos.title: API Versioning Without Breaking Clients: URL vs Header vs Date
videos.summary: Your payments API must switch from dollars to cents, and thousands of partners depend on the old format. This lesson shows how to version an API so nobody breaks overnight.
chapters: 0:00 A breaking change in a payments API
0:46 Three ways to signal the version

videos.title: API Pagination: Offset vs Cursor & Why Deep Pages Are Slow
videos.summary: An infinite-scroll feed with 50 million posts. Does page 500 load in 5 ms or 5 seconds? Do users see duplicates or miss posts? It all depends on how you paginate.

videos.title: API Filtering, Sorting & Field Selection Without Table Scans
videos.summary: GET /products?category=shoes&sort=-price&fields=id,name. Easy to design, and easy to melt your database with. This lesson covers query-parameter conventions and how to keep every filter and sort fast.

videos.title: Idempotency Keys: How Payment APIs Never Charge Twice on Retry
videos.summary: A customer taps Pay, the charge succeeds, but the response times out and the app retries. Without idempotency, they're charged twice. This lesson shows how Stripe-style idempotency keys make retries safe.

videos.title: API Request Validation: Pydantic, 422, Unknown Fields & Size Limits
videos.summary: An invalid email, a negative age, a 50 MB name and a sneaky is_admin field, all in one request. This lesson shows where and how to stop bad input before it reaches your business logic.

videos.title: API Error Handling: 4xx vs 5xx, Problem Details & Retryable Errors
videos.summary: 200 with "error: true", a 500 that leaks your database host, or plain "something went wrong": none of these can be handled by a client. This lesson shows how to design API errors that clients, monitoring and retries can rely on.
chapters: 2:00 Which errors should a client retry?

videos.title: Rate Limiting Algorithms: Token Bucket vs Sliding Window vs Fixed Window
videos.summary: "100 requests per minute per API key, with bursts of 20." Easy to say, but how do you actually count? This lesson compares the five classic rate limiting algorithms on accuracy, memory and burst behavior.

videos.title: Distributed Rate Limiting: Redis, Lua Scripts, 429 Headers & Redis Down?
videos.summary: 30 gateway instances, a limit of 1,000 requests per minute per tenant. If each instance counts alone, a tenant gets 30,000. This lesson shows how to enforce one limit across many servers, and what to do when the shared store fails.

videos.title: Throttling vs Rate Limiting vs Quotas: Free & Paid Tiers, Monthly Limits
videos.summary: Free tier: 1,000 requests a day. Paid tier: 1 million a month. A per-second limit can't enforce that. This lesson explains throttling, rate limiting, load shedding and quotas, and how to build fair, billable API tiers.

videos.title: API Authentication: API Keys vs JWT vs HMAC Signatures vs mTLS
videos.summary: A mobile app, a partner backend, a payment webhook and an internal service all call your API, and each must prove who it is. This lesson compares the five common authentication methods and where each one fits.

videos.title: API Authorization & BOLA: Scopes, Ownership Checks and Where They Live
videos.summary: User 42 has a valid token, calls GET /orders/1001, then changes it to 1002 and reads someone else's order. Authentication worked; authorization didn't. This is BOLA, the #1 risk in the OWASP API Security Top 10.
chapters: 1:32 The fix: check at the data access
2:06 Why not only at the gateway?

videos.title: API Gateway Explained: What Belongs in It, BFFs & Avoiding a SPOF
videos.summary: Twenty microservices, many clients, and every request needs TLS, authentication and rate limiting. Instead of rebuilding that 20 times, you put one front door in front: an API gateway. This lesson covers what it should do, what it must not do, and how to keep it from becoming a single point of failure.
chapters: 2:29 Don't make it a single point of failure

videos.title: Retries, Exponential Backoff & Jitter: How Retries Cause Outages
videos.summary: A dependency returns 503 for two seconds. One retry would fix it, but a thousand clients retrying in lockstep can turn that blip into a 20-minute outage. This lesson shows how to retry safely.

videos.title: API Timeouts & Deadline Propagation: Budgets, gRPC & Cancellation
videos.summary: The gateway gives a request 2 seconds, but every service behind it waits 10. The user gives up while your backend keeps working on an answer nobody will see. This lesson shows how to pick timeout values and propagate deadlines through a call chain.
chapters: 0:00 2 s at the edge, 10 s inside

videos.title: Webhooks: Reliable Delivery, HMAC Signing, Retries & Duplicate Handling
videos.summary: Instead of polling, your payment provider calls you: a webhook. Simple idea, but designing reliable webhook delivery (and a safe receiver) is a classic system design interview question.

videos.title: Async APIs for Long Jobs: 202 Accepted, Job Status, Polling vs Callbacks
videos.summary: A 300-page PDF takes 10 minutes to parse, chunk, embed and index. You can't hold an HTTP request open that long. This lesson shows how to design async APIs for long-running work.
chapters: 0:47 The job is a resource: an operation
